•	 Depression from the illness, which may result in anorexia.
•	 Hyperinflation of the lungs, which causes flattening of the diaphragm and pressure on the 
abdominal cavity during eating, leading to early satiety and problems with swallowing.
•	 Oxyhemoglobin desaturation during eating, which results in increased dyspnea.
•	 Side effects of medications such as nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dysgeusia, dry mouth, and gastric 
irritation. Medications may also increase the need for protein, calcium, vitamin A, and folic acid 
or result in altered serum levels of potassium, magnesium, vitamins, or cholesterol.
